content.comment_body: Hello again, Our clients wish to remotely monitor and adjust temperature settings. A- Is this achievable? B- How can we restrict their access from modifying the program itself? Thank you in advance.
Using the built-in web server is the simplest solution if you only need to show temperature and allow a variable setpoint.
A short demo is available on video. The temperature is visible in the web interface, and you can set the fan's on/off thresholds via the simulated [product_name] display in the browser.
Thanks for sharing that. Does the web server require payment? If so, is there a license fee per user or is it for multiple users?
The web server feature is free and integrated in most recent CPU models.

The web server is built into the [product_name] [article_no], and does not require a license. It mirrors the display and keys of the base module or [product_name] operator devices; virtual keys are accessible. No physical operator device is required for control via web, but only configured message texts are visible.
Alternatively, you can use the [product_name] App. The internet access setup is similar. Hope this helps.
Hello [user_name], Yes, the app seems to meet our requirements, but it's failing to connect. I entered the web address and only see 'Connection in Progress.' Any ideas?
Have you enabled access through Access Control?
Thank you! When viewing via the web server, should I see what appears on both the base unit display and operator device?
Only programmed message texts are displayed; system menus do not appear in the web interface.
On the web server, you can display the same information as shown on the operator device or PLC display, or customize what is visible only on the web interface.
@[user_name], that's incorrect. On the operator device or base display you can see system menus, but not on the web server. Only programmed messages are shown.

@[user_name], that's not accurate. System menus are visible on the operator device or base display, not via web server. Only programmed messages appear there. I specifically meant that the web server can present certain information that's not shown on the controller. When I set up the web server, I could monitor input/output status and control them from my PC.
Everything is resolved, thanks everyone! Now, it's time for the next challenge.
A new thread has been created for [user_name]'s question on GSM/GPRS in [product_name] [version_no]. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are looking for simple solutions to remotely monitor and adjust temperature settings using web interfaces and mobile apps for [product_name] systems. The integrated web server and app offer these features without requiring paid licenses, which is appreciated. Some users are facing connection issues with the app and have questions about access control and display options, suggesting a need for clearer configuration guidance.
analysis.user_expectations: Clients should be able to remotely view and edit temperature settings easily, but without full programming access. Clear instructions on licensing, user restrictions, and configuration are expected.
